script_fix: endcard-treat.sh had The Chain's values hardcoded (EXPECT=299.0, FADE_START=295.152, audio probes at t=240/280/295) — all past the end of a 230s song, so it refused to run. Now an array. Failing closed was correct behaviour; if this error appears on a file you trust, check the splitting before hunting in Resolve.

schedule_rationale: Dean asked for morning; per-platform research says LinkedIn peaks 8am-12pm AEST (commute 7-9am) and Facebook 8-10am, but Instagram peaks 5-10pm and TikTok later still. Rather than spend the best LinkedIn day of the week on its worst hour for two platforms, the burst was SPLIT: morning for YouTube/LinkedIn/Facebook, evening for Instagram/TikTok. Dean approved. thumbnail_upload_trick: Thumbnails are all under 10MB, so the Chrome extension's file_upload tool CAN set them — target the hidden input[type=file] via find/JS rather than clicking the visible button, which opens a blocking native dialog. Worked for YouTube (id 'file-loader') and TikTok's Edit cover. It does NOT work for LinkedIn, whose thumbnail input does not exist in the DOM until that blocking click happens — that one stays Dean's.
file_upload_scope: file_upload refuses paths outside the session's own directories. Copy the thumbnail into the scratchpad first.
tiktok_toast_lies: TikTok showed 'Video published' after a SCHEDULE action and redirected to the Posts list. It was scheduled correctly. Same class as the YouTube toast already in the runbook — verify in the list, never trust the toast.
tiktok_time_picker: The hour column advances ONE step per scroll gesture regardless of scroll_amount, and typing into the field is rejected. 24 scrolls is not viable. What works: find the two scrollable columns in the DOM, set scrollTop = hour*32 and minute_index*32, dispatch a 'scroll' event, then CLICK the centred value in each column to commit — setting scrollTop alone leaves the field unchanged.
youtube_time_picker: Same shape: 'End, backspace x6, type, Tab' silently reverts. The field is a combobox — type the value, then click the matching option in the dropdown list (found via JS, it is virtualised out of the a11y tree).
